title: Punjab Chemicals & Crop Protection Ltd-$ - 506618 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 8.7% YoY to INR347.2 crores, with EBITDA up 18.8% to INR40.8 crores at an 11.8% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR347.2 crores, up 8.7% YoY from INR319.5 crores, with gross margin at 36.6% (up 355 bps) and EBITDA of INR40.8 crores (11.8% margin). PAT was INR22.1 crores, up 7% YoY, a 6.4% margin. Management said Indian agrochemical demand is weak from delayed sowing and a weak monsoon, with pricing pressure in India and adverse European weather delaying buying. Q1 growth was driven by exports (up 27.7%) on better inventory planning, while domestic revenue fell 3.1%. Management reiterated its guidance of 15-20% revenue growth for FY27 and a 15% EBITDA margin over 2-3 years, with H2 expected to be stronger.

financial_highlights.metric: One-time employee cost (long-term benefits and appraisal)

financial_highlights.value: Rose from 62 to 71 days in FY26 (per analyst); no Q1 figure given
financial_highlights.change: Expected to rise further in FY27 before returning to range in Q4

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Agrochemicals are about 65-70% of the portfolio and will remain dominant. Europe is about 70% of export revenue, with the rest from US, Latin America and Japan.

segments.name: Specialty and pharma (new products)
segments.commentary: New products contributed about 14% of Q1 revenue and grew about 40% YoY (per analyst). FY27 target is 15-18% of revenue, with 4-5 products commercialised per year.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: CDMO is about 50:50 with catalog products. Management expects 2-3 more multi-year customers to sign within 2-3 quarters, with Japanese and European talks ongoing.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (food-grade phosphoric acid)
segments.commentary: Supplies leading global beverage companies in India, with more customers added over the last two quarters. Segment margin is targeted to improve over 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20% is maintained, with H2 expected to deliver at least 15-20% growth, as H1 is seasonally strong.
EBITDA margin is expected to improve gradually through the year; 15% EBITDA margin target is maintained over the next 2-3 years.
New products targeted at 15-18% of FY27 revenue, rising above 20% next year.

Two MoU products expected to ramp from Q4 FY27 after customer approval; two herbicide intermediates to launch this year, each contributing about INR10-20 crores in year one and INR40-50 crores at peak in 2-4 years.
Greenfield capex expected to start in FY27; Lalru block work is progressing and completion is targeted this financial year.
Management indicated the FY26 revenue base was about INR1,030 crores; 15-18% growth implies about INR1,200 crores.
capex_capacity: Derabassi utilisation was about 85% in Q1; Lalru was about 71-72%. Both are expected to improve in Q2 and Q3.
The debottlenecked agrochemical intermediate has reached design capacity after the last-quarter shutdown, and is expected to add significantly to revenue and profit this year.
New manufacturing block at Lalru: civil work has started, with more investment in Q2 and Q3 for completion this financial year.
A pilot plant revamp to scale up several products at once is targeted for completion in September-October 2026.
A new manufacturing site is being evaluated for long-term agro and specialty growth; details to follow.
demand_pricing: Indian agrochemical demand is weak due to delayed sowing and a weak monsoon, with visible pricing pressure in India.
Europe demand is seeing price pressure more than volume pressure; management expects a 5-8% demand reduction and is securing contracts with dynamic pricing.
Growth in Q1 exports came from inventory built in Q4 FY26 for H1 demand, per management. A peer reportedly saw export volume declines.
Price increases contributed about 3-4% of the 9% revenue growth; the rest came from volume.
Raw material spot prices were volatile due to solvent and chemical availability and Middle East tensions affecting feedstock, energy and freight.
Management reports customers in Europe and Japan and in India are seeking China-plus-one sourcing from India, but Japanese conversions take longer.
Top 5 customers contribute 60-65% of revenue and top 10 about 75%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 9% revenue growth came from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-4% came from price increases and the balance from volume.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital cycle reverse from the 71 days in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days will rise during the year because of seasonal products, and return to around last year's level by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the employee cost high and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a one-time long-term benefit and appraisal reward to 3 people, worth about INR4-4.5 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Has the commercialisation timeline of the three MoU products shifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Two products have had commercial lots supplied; customer testing takes 3-6 months, so ramp-up is expected in coming quarters after approval. The MoU products are not in commercial scale yet.

qa_highlights.question: Does management maintain the 15% EBITDA margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, over 2-3 years, via process improvements and novel technologies for higher-margin products. Q1 raw material price volatility made the market tough.

qa_highlights.question: Is the herbicide intermediate revenue potential unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Each of two products is expected to contribute INR10-20 crores in launch year, reaching INR40-50 crores per annum at peak in 2-4 years.

risks_watch: Europe demand could fall 5-8% and pricing pressure is expected to persist; monitor Q2 volumes and realisations.
Domestic revenue declined 3.1% in Q1, with weak Indian monsoon and sowing delays; watch for recovery.
Q1 export growth was driven by Q4 inventory build, so H2 export volumes may not repeat it.
MoU products rely on customer approvals; ramp-up from Q4 FY27 is not yet confirmed.
Working capital days are set to rise in FY27 before recovering by Q4.
Raw material and freight costs are volatile due to Middle East tensions, solvent availability and dependence on China imports.
Generic product pressure from Chinese competitors as patents expire.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term and H2 outlook, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing. Management was evasive on the margin split between price, mix and efficiency, and on the contribution of individual new products.
key_quotes: We expect our EBITDA margin to improve gradually as the year progresses.
So far signals are on the price pressure, not on the volume side.
Pricing is market-driven. So say, for example, we got some advantage in pricing in Q1, that may not be sustainable because we have to adjust to the market conditions.

growth.why: Management maintained FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%) and expects H2 to deliver at least 15-20%, backed by a debottlenecked intermediate at design capacity, two herbicide intermediates and two MoU products ramping from Q4, and CDMO wins; however, the Lalru block is 3 quarters out, Q1 domestic revenue fell 3.1%, Indian demand is weak, and the H2 pickup is only partly evidenced with s

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose 355 bps to 36.6% and EBITDA margin is 11.8%, but management was evasive on price vs mix vs efficiency, Q1 raw material volatility was high, and the 15% target is 2-3 years out versus 11.8% today.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Lalru new manufacturing block has civil work started with completion targeted this financial year (Q3-Q4 FY27), and the debottlenecked intermediate is already at design capacity; Lalru utilisation is only 71-72%, so the new block is not a near-term need.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 growth was mostly volume (3-4% price of 9% growth), but it was pulled forward by Q4 FY26 export inventory build, domestic revenue fell 3.1%, and Europe expects 5-8% demand reduction.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Derabassi utilisation is about 85% (above the 80% threshold) and a new manufacturing site is under evaluation with details to follow, so a capex announcement is likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 growth at 15-20% but Q1 growth was only 8.7%, domestic fell 3.1% and Europe demand is weakening, so an upgrade is unlikely before H2 proves out.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver at least 15-20% growth to hit FY27 guidance of 15-20% (FY26 base about INR1,030 crores, target about INR1,200 crores), while H1 growth was 8.7% and Indian demand and European pricing are weak.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two MoU products ramp from Q4 FY27 after customer approval, two herbicide intermediates launch this year (INR10-20 crores each in year one), and new products were about 14% of Q1 revenue, targeted at 15-18% for FY27.

rows.label: Working capital days rise before reversing
rows.why: Working capital days rose from 62 to 71 in FY26 and are expected to rise further during FY27 before returning to last year's level by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: CDMO multi-year customer wins
rows.why: Management expects 2-3 more multi-year CDMO customers to sign within 2-3 quarters, with Japanese and European talks ongoing, though Japanese conversions take longer.

rows.label: China-plus-one sourcing shift
rows.why: Customers in Europe, Japan and India are seeking China-plus-one sourcing from India, but Japanese conversions take longer and top 5 customers already make up 60-65% of revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term and H2 outlook, the Lalru block and the 15% margin target, but cautious on near-term Indian demand and European pricing; analysts pushed on the 9% growth split between price and volume and on the one-time employee cost.
